{{nihongo|'''Takeuchi Shrine'''|武内神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kōzuke Province]].

===History===
It is said that the shrine originated from being divided from {{ill|Kawasukune Shrine (Shibukawa)|Q66085130|qid=Q66085130|lt=Kawanami no Sukune Shrine}} in Kawashima on September 21 of the 1st year of {{ill|Bun'an|Q1193586|qid=Q1193586}} ({{ill|1444|Q6420|qid=Q6420}}){{Sfn|Gunma Prefecture Gunma District Education Association|1925|p=587}}{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=883-884}}.

As indicated by a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōgen senji}} from the 5th year of {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} (1708) that records the name “Shōichi-i Sukune Daimyōjin,” the shrine was known as “Sukune Shrine” until the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}}), it was renamed “Takeuchi Shrine”{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=883-884}}. The {{ill|biane|Q5358873|qid=Q5358873}} on the {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} bears the inscription “Shōichi-i Sukune Daimyōjin.”

{{ill|Kisao Ozaki|Q21698487|qid=Q21698487}} proposed that Takeuchi Shrine (Sukune Shrine) was originally Kawanami no Sukune Shrine. He interpreted “Kawanami” as “river” and “Sukune” as “chokune,” understanding the shrine name to mean “the main current of the river.” He explained that because three shrines—{{ill|Kawasukune Shrine (Higashiagatsuma)|Q66085131|qid=Q66085131|lt=Hakoshima}}, Obashima, and Kawashima—were lined up along the {{ill|Agatsuma River|Q1636255|qid=Q1636255}} in places with “shima” (island) in their names, they represented the deification of the Agatsuma River itself.<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Studies on the Jinmyōchō of Kōzuke Province |date=1974-12-10 |year=1974 |publisher=Ozaki Sensei Chosho Kankōkai |pages=210-212 |last=Ozaki |author=Kizao Ozaki |first=Kizao |author-link=Kizao Ozaki |doi=10.11501/12266236}}{{Registration required}}</ref>

An engraved inscription dated the 8th year of {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} ({{ill|1711|Q6866|qid=Q6866}}) is found on the {{ill|Giboshi|Q3105399|qid=Q3105399}} of the balustrade of the main hall, and thus that year is considered the year of construction{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=883-884}}.

The shrine buildings are located atop a high ground known as Ubazuka{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=883-884}}. Although it was once thought to be a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718}}, it is in fact a natural {{ill|Hügelland|Q222912|qid=Q222912}}{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|p=117}}. There is a local tradition that this was the place where {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}}’s wife {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Uwagitsuhime}} and their child lived, and that Ubazuka is the grave of Uwagitsuhime, which is said to be the origin of the place name Obashima{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1984|p=903}}.

===Festivals===
* April 3 – Spring annual festival{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|p=542}}
* July 25 – Gion Festival; a festival of the enshrined Yasaka Shrine, during which a portable shrine is paraded{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|p=542}}.
* October 9 – Autumn annual festival{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|p=542}}

===Access===
* 10-minute walk from {{ill|Ubashima Station|Q7876424|qid=Q7876424}} on the {{ill|Agatsuma Line|Q391568|qid=Q391568}} of {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}}
